summary: Building and measuring LLM inference and training, from phone NPUs to datacenter GPUs and AI accelerators.

highlights: Shipped **OpenWeights** to Google Play; its on-device ExecuTorch LFM2.5 1.2B decodes **2.3× faster** than llama.cpp on Tensor G5.
Shipped **ExecuServe**, an OpenAI-compatible Android LLM server; Qwen3-1.7B's first token took **0.41 s** on NPU vs. 2.0 s on CPU.
Built KV cache prefix reuse on Android; Qwen3-1.7B's second turn prefilled in **215 ms** by feeding 20 new tokens, not all 1,212.
Merged a fix into **PyTorch ExecuTorch** that stops LFM2 models from carrying state into a new conversation.
Traced lost tool calls in int4 LFM2.5 phone builds to weight rounding; GPTQ lifted search recall **10% to 49%** in held-out evals.
Published **236 ExecuTorch builds of 21 LLMs** for phone CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs.
Ran 9 LLMs in every CPU/GPU/NPU prefill-decode pairing on Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5; NPU prefill was **9.6–15.5×** faster than CPU.
Traced decode stalls on throttled phones (23.3 to **0.35 tok/s**) to spinning llama.cpp threads and added a 2-thread fallback in C++.
Built a filing-eligibility engine for **25 state registries**, with live-lookup latency of 2.7 s p50 and 9.2 s p95 in 20 states.
Built Delaware, Mississippi and Indiana registry scrapers that collected **4.9M+ business records** and 387,748 filing PDFs.
Built SMTP verification and fleet autoscaling for a team email-discovery pipeline that processed **1.6M+ records**.
Delivered a patient-search AI system for a hospital in **30 days** using Google Cloud, Vertex AI, and AlloyDB.
